target_customer: Office managers and operations teams at tech companies, with employees as requesters
problem: Software had improved work for most employees but not for office operations teams, who handled requests by chat and email. Hivy gave them a task system and employee helpdesk.
product_category: Office operations task management and employee helpdesk

founders.name: Pauline Tordeur
founders.background_notes: Handled customer support per TechCrunch. Technical status inferred from role only, so treat as unverified.

exit.reason: Managed by Q's first acquisition; price undisclosed; Hivy core team joined Managed by Q.

competitors.name: Managed by Q
competitors.what: Office management marketplace and services for offices; French press called it Hivy's competitor
competitors.traction_then: Shared many customers with Hivy per its CEO in 2017

competitors.name: Envoy
competitors.what: Visitor management used in offices; one user review says it was used before Hivy

technical_complexity.rationale: A request and task workflow tool with chat and email integrations is standard SaaS engineering for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Task history and workflows gave some lock in but general task tools and a service player could cover the same need.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Managed by Q bought Hivy in September 2017 and later was itself acquired by WeWork in 2019.

market_need_then: Hexa says Hivy reached first product-market fit in 2016 with accounts such as Slack and Typeform, and YC advised that scaling would need a service beyond software.

branding.name_origin: Hexa says the product began as Tipi, an app store for the office, and was renamed Hivy for trademark reasons.
branding.domain_note: Used hivyapp.com, not hivy.com; the site now shows Nothing Found for deep pages.
branding.community_and_virality: Launched on Product Hunt in April 2016 and was reported as number 2 product of the day by one source.

brand_strength.rationale: A hive-like name that fits team work, but similar Hive names exist, searches return other products, and no brand press was found.

pivots.from: Tipi, an app store for the office
pivots.to: Task management and helpdesk for office operations teams
pivots.why: Narrowed for business reasons per Hexa

outcome_analysis: Hivy narrowed from an office app store to a task tool for office operations, found early fit with large tech accounts in 2016, and joined YC in January 2017. YC feedback was that scaling needed a service layer and a large seed. Instead of raising, the founders sold to Managed by Q in September 2017, which shared customers and offered services. Price and funding are not public.
notes: No funding information found in two searches, so rounds are empty and not a statement of zero. Hexa says Hivy was in its HX16 batch; one search summary mentioned 2016 as an acquisition year but TechCrunch dates it September 2017. The Managed by Q competitor source is dated at the acquisition, not at founding. Founder backgrounds not found. Hivy site homepage fetch returned only a Nothing Found page.
